sections.heading: the agreement
body: These terms are an agreement between you and Ummi Labs, LLC ("we"), the operator of the soot app and the servers it uses by default. By creating an identity, signing in with a key, or browsing without an account, you agree to them and to the community guidelines. If you do not agree, do not use soot.
You must be at least 17 years old to use soot.

sections.heading: what soot is
body: soot is a client for Nostr, an open network. Your account is a key pair that you hold. We do not have your secret key, cannot reset it and cannot recover it. Keep a backup.

soot shows content from our own relay and servers and from relays run by other people. We moderate what our servers carry. We do not control other relays, and what they hold is governed by their operators.

sections.heading: your content
body: You own what you post. You give us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to store, transmit, transcode and display it so the service can work, for as long as it remains on our servers.
Posts you publish are public and are copied to relays we do not run. Deleting them sends a deletion request; relays and people who already hold a copy may keep it.

sections.heading: music and media you upload
body: You may only upload music, artwork and other media that you made or that you have the rights to distribute. By uploading you confirm that you hold those rights, including the rights in any samples, and that the upload does not infringe anyone's copyright, trademark, privacy or publicity rights.
You are responsible for what you upload. We remove uploads when we receive a valid claim, and we close the accounts of people who infringe repeatedly.

sections.heading: no tolerance for objectionable content or abuse
body: There is no tolerance on soot for objectionable content or abusive users. The community guidelines say what that covers. We remove content that breaks them from our servers and we remove the people who post it, and we act on reports within 24 hours.
You can report any post, message, track, profile or voice participant from inside the app, and you can block anyone. Blocking hides that person from you immediately.

sections.heading: copyright claims
body: If you believe something on soot infringes your copyright, write to copyright@thewired.app with: what the work is; where it appears in soot (a link, or the track and artist name); your contact details; a statement that you believe in good faith the use is not authorised; a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the notice is accurate and that you are the owner or act for the owner; and your signature, typed or otherwise.
If your upload was removed by mistake you can send a counter-notice to the same address. We will pass it to the person who made the claim.
Our designated agent is registered with the US Copyright Office. The full notice and counter-notice process is at thewired.app/dmca.

sections.heading: tips
body: Zaps are voluntary tips sent from your own Lightning wallet to another person. They buy nothing: no content, feature or access is unlocked by tipping. We never hold your funds, we take no fee, and we cannot reverse a payment.

sections.heading: the assistant
body: Navi uses an AI provider that you choose and connect with your own key. What you send to it goes from your device to that provider under their terms. soot asks before anything is sent.

sections.heading: deleting your account
body: You can delete your account in settings, under account & security. That blanks your profile, asks relays to erase what you published, and removes your key and data from the device. The full process is at thewired.app/delete-account. For anything held on our servers you can also write to privacy@thewired.app.

sections.heading: ending access
body: We may remove content from our servers or stop serving an account that breaks these terms or the guidelines, with or without notice. You can stop using soot at any time.

sections.heading: no warranty, limited liability
body: soot is provided as it is. To the extent the law allows, we give no warranties, and we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for lost keys or funds, or for content posted by other people.

sections.heading: changes and law
body: We may change these terms. When the meaning changes we will ask you to agree again. These terms are governed by the law of the State of Delaware, United States.
Questions: support@thewired.app.

sections.heading: the short version
body: soot is for music and the people around it. Post what is yours, leave people alone when they ask, and do not use the place to hurt anyone.

sections.heading: not allowed
body: Sexual content involving minors, or anything that sexualises them. We report it to the authorities.
Threats, harassment, stalking, and encouraging others to harm themselves or anyone else.
Hate directed at people for their race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability or origin.
Sexually explicit media that is not marked as sensitive, and any sexual media shared without the consent of the people in it.
Content that promotes or organises violence or terrorism, or that is illegal where it is posted.
Other people's private information.
Spam, scams, malware and impersonation.
Music or media you do not have the rights to.

sections.heading: what happens
body: Reports are read by a person. We act within 24 hours: the content comes off our servers and the account that posted it is removed from them. Serious or repeated abuse is permanent.
Spaces have their own moderators, who can set stricter rules. They cannot set looser ones.

sections.heading: reporting and blocking
body: Press and hold any post, message, track or person to report or block. Blocking is immediate and private.
You can also write to abuse@thewired.app.

sections.heading: the short version
body: You can delete your soot account from inside the app. Open the you tab, then settings, then account & security, and press delete account. Deletion is permanent.
If you no longer have the app, write to privacy@thewired.app with your public key (your npub) and we will remove what our servers hold.

sections.heading: in the app
body: Go to settings, then account & security. Under danger zone, press delete account and confirm. If this account created spaces, the app asks whether to hand them to their admins or delete them too. Deleted spaces are gone for every member.
There is no password and no cooling-off period. Your account is a key pair that only you hold, so once the key is removed from your device there is no way back in.

sections.heading: what our servers remove
body: Ummi Labs, LLC runs the soot app's default servers at thewired.app. When you delete your account they remove: your uploads and the streaming versions we made of them, your releases and playlists, our copy of your profile and your verified handle, your space memberships, roles and invites, your push devices and notification settings, your play history and recommendations, and everything you published to our relay up to the moment of the request, including encrypted messages addressed to you.
Deletion starts as soon as our servers accept the request and finishes on its own. Deleted data can survive in a database backup for up to about three months before it is gone for good.

sections.heading: what we keep
body: A record that you asked, which is the signed request itself, so nothing from the deleted account can be re-published to our servers. Moderation records such as reports and bans in spaces that still exist, and reports you filed, with your key removed from them. Aggregate counts such as plays, which do not identify you.

sections.heading: what is published to other relays
body: soot is a client for Nostr, an open network, so your posts also live on relays run by other people. Before the app removes your key it publishes two signed events: a blank profile, which replaces your name, picture and bio wherever the newest profile wins, and a request to vanish, which asks every relay to erase what this account published and to refuse copies of it afterwards.
Relays and apps run by other people decide for themselves whether to honour that request. Some may keep copies, and anyone who already saved a copy of a public post still has it.

sections.heading: what leaves this device
body: The account's secret key and everything it left on the phone: messages, drafts, downloads, assistant chats and the wallet connection. If other accounts are signed in on the device, they stay.

sections.heading: without the app
body: Write to privacy@thewired.app from any address, with the public key of the account (the npub, or the hex key). We remove what our servers hold, as listed above, and reply when it is done.
We cannot publish the request to vanish for you, because only your secret key can sign it. If you still have the key, any Nostr app that supports requests to vanish can send one.
